entries.rootCause: The skill described localization as a generic five-step checklist but did not tell the agent to make a supplied contract/output ABI the authoritative boundary, derive outputs from confirmed markers, or perform a single robust verification pass. As a result, the run repeatedly rediscovered scope, used the report example as an implicit schema, and spent several attempts on fragile PowerShell quoting even though the final artifact was correct.
entries.reasoning: Evidence 0 is a clean run (runStatus=ok) with no quality score, so it is usable workflow evidence but not proof of a scored defect. The trace shows the agent succeeded, yet it made repeated reads/listings, attempted three brittle PowerShell checks that failed at parse time, and only later converged on a simpler string/field verification that passed. The source contract explicitly defined allowed/protected files, confirmed-text semantics, exact keys, required outputs, and a closed report ABI, while the original skill did not instruct the agent to prioritize such a contract or distinguish its machine-readable ABI from the illustrative Markdown report. I therefore rewrote the existing workflow in place rather than appending overlapping rules. The change is general: any future React, Vue, or other localization task with a project contract benefits from authoritative scope and ABI handling; any task with a shell-based verification benefits from quoting guidance. The rewrite-in-place test is satisfied because the vague original five steps were replaced directly. The coherent scope is one concise documentation edit; no new executable is justified because the evidence contains semantic translation choices and no reusable source processor. There are no PASSING tasks in PER_TASK_SUMMARY.md, so there is no scored passing contract to regress; the edit preserves the original framework coverage and leaves translation quality, pluralization, and unsupported contract details as agent duties. Expected impact is reduced exploratory I/O and fewer false verification failures while preserving the successful transformation behavior. Opportunities are separated: artifact production covers the declared config/locales/report and source wiring; verification covers ABI/key/file checks; environment dependency covers shell portability. Repeated transformation is retained because the trace demonstrates repeated reads and retries but does not expose a reusable general processor boundary. The candidate is the SKILL.md rewrite; the recommendation retains semantic judgment with the agent and requires contract-driven validation when available.

changes.description: Replaced the generic checklist with contract-first scope discovery, confirmed-text derivation, exact ABI-aware artifact generation, allowed-file preservation, and one robust verification pass.
changes.generality: A future Vue-i18n task with a locale contract and a future batch localization task with a closed report schema would both benefit from the same contract-first workflow.

inputs: actual source files in task scope
outputs: localized source files within allowed scope
preconditions: the agent can read the supplied project files
the contract or framework rules define the applicable boundary

constraints.description: Use exact contract keys and output fields when a contract exists; do not add plausible schema fields.
The observed task's allowed/protected/required paths and exact ABI are task-scoped evidence, not permanent filenames or values.
The source run used a PowerShell environment; shell syntax must be adapted to the current environment.

residualDuties: Choose translation wording and semantic mappings
Handle unsupported formats or ambiguous scope explicitly
Do not treat self-verification as proof of translation quality
verification: Confirm the workflow instructions are in the original five workflow sections
Confirm no task-specific filenames or values were added to SKILL.md

bestRoundReason: optimized draft has no concrete local program failure but remains partially or wholly unvalidated
